t: You're looking at the memorial to Charles Fryatt, inside Liverpool Street station. Fryatt was a British merchant seaman. In 1915 he tried to ram a German U-boat with his ship, the SS Brussels. The following year the Germans captured the Brussels off occupied Belgium, court-martialled him for illegal civilian warfare, and sentenced him to death. He was shot by firing squad near Bruges. In 1919 his body was brought home and reburied with honours. The memorial shows him and was made by the sculptor H. T. H. van Golberdinge.
